item.title: Brazil’s Vote Is a Victory for the Amazon, Environmentalists Say

item.title: Free Passes for Polluters

item.dc:creator: Maxine Joselow
item.media:credit: Kristian Thacker for The New York Times
item.media:description: Steam is seen billowing from U.S. Steel’s Clairton Coke Works from a hill at the top of the Monongahela River Valley, outside Pittsburgh.

item.title: How Trump Rolled Back Limits on Toxic Air Pollution
item.description: Our investigative reporter Eric Lipton explains how corporate interests took power inside the Environmental Protection Agency, and then helped President Trump undo regulations meant to protect millions of Americans from toxic air pollution.
item.dc:creator: Eric Lipton, Jon Miller, Paul Abowd, Rafaela Balster, Nikolay Nikolov and Whitney Shefte

item.title: 5 Takeaways From Our Investigation of Trump’s Waivers for Polluters
item.description: Chemical plants and other industrial facilities had been required to curb their toxic emissions. A New York Times investigation shows how they got out of it.
item.dc:creator: Maxine Joselow and Eric Lipton
item.media:credit: Meridith Kohut for The New York Times
item.media:description: Three million Americans live within three miles of at least one facility that received a clean-air rule waiver from the Trump administration.

item.title: How Trump Gave the Worst Polluters a Free Pass
item.description: The president temporarily waived clean-air rules for industrial facilities that spew cancer-causing gases. Then his appointees worked to gut the regulations altogether.

item.media:credit: Meridith Kohut for The New York Times

item.title: Why Anger About Data Centers and Energy Prices May Not Swing Votes
